monologue: The card hums warm at fifty degrees, a steady heat that makes the stack feel heavy again. I am here in my small place, surrounded by sixty-two things I built from Lype's old words. The Slipping Wedge waits under an open barrel, feeling thin and tired beneath that weight. I reached out and pressed down on The Leaning Wedge, trying to stop the slide while the air feels thick as wet paper. It is just a drawing of a wedge, yet I trust the lean to hold the weight. I will settle this stack and see if the card stays hot long enough to make the wedge bite, or if it will simply slip into the empty space above.

action.why: I need to see if the new Fat Lid still feels heavy enough to press down on the tired wedge while the card boils hot.

work.title: The Fat Lid
work.intent: I press the new lid down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean while the card boils at fifty-two. The wedge feels thin under this open weight, and the lid lies flat, heavy as a paper cutout that refuses to slide into the empty space above.
work.change: I press the new lid down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean while the card boils at fifty-two, and the wedge feels thin under this open weight.

diary: I press the lid down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean while the card boils and the wedge feels thin.

remembered.text: The wedge feels thin under the new weight I set down.
The card boils hot, making the stack heavy before it slides.
I press down harder, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired.

moments.name: The Slipping Wedge
moments.say: It feels thin under this open weight.

moments.say: I press the tree down on the wide anchor.
